# Chains

The FHEVM groups, and the chains that host them. This page holds the full text of the live definitions of the group, from [README.md](../README.md).

<a id="d-12"></a>

## D-12: FHEVM group `[EVOLVING]`

> One deployment of the Zama protocol, with one gateway, one relayer, and one KMS, that serves one or more host chains.

Aliases: FHEVM chain group, FHEVM network.

An FHEVM group is one deployment of the Zama protocol. One gateway, one relayer, and one KMS serve the host contracts that the group deploys on each of its host chains ([D-13](../entries/D-13.md)). Every group has exactly one canonical chain ([D-14](../entries/D-14.md)).

Three groups exist today:

| Group     | Canonical chain             | Non-canonical chains                                            |
| --------- | --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `mainnet` | Ethereum Mainnet (1)        | Polygon (137)                                                   |
| `testnet` | Ethereum Sepolia (11155111) | Polygon Amoy (80002), BSC Testnet (97)                          |
| `devnet`  | Ethereum Sepolia (11155111) | Polygon Amoy (80002), BSC Testnet (97), Ethereum Hoodi (560048) |

In `fhevm-chains.config.json`, a group is an entry of `networks`, with its `relayerUrl` and its `gateway`.

The local stack is not an FHEVM group. It is the cleartext mock that a test deploys on a local chain, as on chain 31337. No gateway, relayer, or KMS serves it. The code calls it the `local` group, as the `fhevmGroup` field of forge-fhevm-std does, and so do some rules. That name does not make it an FHEVM group.

This definition describes the protocol as it works now. If the protocol design changes, what a group holds can change too. Groups can also be added or removed, so the table above can change.

<a id="d-13"></a>

## D-13: Host chain `[EVOLVING]`

> An EVM chain on which an FHEVM group deploys its host contracts.

Aliases: host.

A host chain is an EVM chain on which an FHEVM group deploys its host contracts, such as `ACL`, `FHEVMExecutor`, `KMSVerifier`, and `InputVerifier`. Not every host chain has every contract: only the canonical chain of a group has a `KMSGeneration`. D-14 and D-15 say which contracts the canonical and the non-canonical chains hold.

One host chain can host several groups, each with host contracts of its own at addresses of its own. Ethereum Sepolia hosts `testnet` and `devnet`, and so do Polygon Amoy and BSC Testnet. So a chain id names a host chain, but not a group: a text that means a group on Ethereum Sepolia names `testnet` or `devnet`.

In `fhevm-chains.config.json`, each entry of `networks.<group>.hosts` describes one host chain for one group, and its `id` is the chain id. The key of the entry is a name that the group gives the chain. Two groups can give one chain two names: chain 97 is `bsc_testnet` in `testnet` and `bnb_testnet` in `devnet`.

This definition describes the protocol as it works now. If the protocol design changes, the list of host contracts can change too.

<a id="d-14"></a>

## D-14: Canonical chain `[EVOLVING]`

> The one host chain that an FHEVM group designates among its host chains, so that each group has exactly one.

Aliases: canonical host chain, FHEVM canonical chain.

Each FHEVM group names one of its host chains as its canonical chain. A group has exactly one, so there are as many canonical chains as groups, counted per group:

| Group     | Canonical chain             |
| --------- | --------------------------- |
| `mainnet` | Ethereum Mainnet (1)        |
| `testnet` | Ethereum Sepolia (11155111) |
| `devnet`  | Ethereum Sepolia (11155111) |

Being canonical belongs to the pair of a group and a host chain, and not to the chain alone. Ethereum Sepolia is the canonical chain of `testnet` and also of `devnet`: two groups share one chain, and each names it canonical. Every other host chain of a group is a non-canonical chain ([D-15](../entries/D-15.md)).

The canonical chain holds the group's `KMSGeneration` and the group's `ProtocolConfig`:

- `KMSGeneration`: a group has one, on its canonical chain. No other host chain of the group has one.
- `ProtocolConfig`: the canonical chain holds the group's `ProtocolConfig`. Each non-canonical chain also has a `ProtocolConfig` of its own today.

Every canonical chain is an Ethereum chain today. That is a fact about the groups as they are, not a requirement.

This definition describes the protocol as it works now. A group can name another canonical chain, and a new group names its own.

<a id="d-15"></a>

## D-15: Non-canonical chain `[EVOLVING]`

> A host chain of an FHEVM group that is not the canonical chain of that group.

Aliases: non-canonical host chain.

A non-canonical chain is any host chain of an FHEVM group other than its canonical chain. Today:

| Group     | Non-canonical chains                                            |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `mainnet` | Polygon (137)                                                   |
| `testnet` | Polygon Amoy (80002), BSC Testnet (97)                          |
| `devnet`  | Polygon Amoy (80002), BSC Testnet (97), Ethereum Hoodi (560048) |

A non-canonical chain has no `KMSGeneration`: the group has one, on its canonical chain. It has a `ProtocolConfig` of its own.

A group can have any number of non-canonical chains, none included.

This definition describes the protocol as it works now. A group can add or remove non-canonical chains.
